group: Valid inputs – absolute URI with JSON node

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema instance whose meta‑schema matches the default version
cases.description: When a proper absolute SchemaLocation and a valid JsonNode are supplied, getSchema should create a JsonSchema without throwing and the returned object should be usable for validation.

group: Valid inputs – relative URI with JSON node

cases.description: Relative URIs are resolved by the factory; the method should still return a JsonSchema instance.

group: Null schemaUri – should raise NPE

cases.description: The method requires a non‑null SchemaLocation; passing null must result in a NullPointerException.

group: Null jsonNode – schema loaded from location

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema instance loaded from the supplied location
cases.description: When jsonNode is null the factory should read the schema from the provided SchemaLocation and still return a JsonSchema.

group: Both parameters null – should raise NPE

cases.description: Both arguments being null is illegal; the method must throw a NullPointerException before any processing.

group: Invalid URI format – malformed schemaUri

cases.description: A malformed URI should cause the factory to reject the SchemaLocation and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Empty JSON node – schema without content

cases.expected: returns a JsonSchema instance whose root node is empty (no validation rules)
cases.description: Even an empty JsonNode is a valid input; the method should still construct a JsonSchema object.

group: Valid inputs – schemaUri with fragment and null jsonNode

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema instance whose root node corresponds to the fragment definition
cases.description: When the supplied SchemaLocation contains a fragment that points to a definition inside the schema and jsonNode is null, the factory must load the schema, resolve the fragment and return a usable JsonSchema object.

group: Invalid schemaUri – unsupported scheme (mailto)

cases.description: The factory only supports http, https, file and classpath schemes. Supplying a mailto URI should cause an IllegalArgumentException.

group: Non‑existent classpath resource – should raise IllegalArgumentException

cases.description: When jsonNode is null the factory tries to read the schema from the given classpath location. If the resource does not exist, an IllegalArgumentException (or a subclass) must be thrown.

group: jsonNode is an array node – should raise IllegalArgumentException

cases.description: A JSON Schema must be a JSON object. Supplying an array node as the schema definition is illegal and the factory should reject it with an IllegalArgumentException.

group: schemaUri with encoded spaces – should succeed

cases.description: URIs containing percent‑encoded spaces are valid. The method must correctly handle them and produce a JsonSchema.

group: schemaUri with query parameters – should succeed

cases.description: Query strings are allowed in a SchemaLocation. The factory should ignore the query part for loading the schema and still return a valid JsonSchema.

group: jsonNode with $ref to external schema – should resolve external reference

cases.expected: returns a non‑null JsonSchema instance whose validation includes the referenced external schema
cases.description: When the supplied JsonNode contains a $ref that points to another schema (classpath URI), the factory must load the referenced schema and incorporate it, resulting in a fully resolved JsonSchema.

group: schemaUri with trailing slash – should succeed

cases.description: A URI ending with a slash is still a valid location. The method must not treat it as an error and should create a JsonSchema.

group: Invalid JSON content at schemaUri – malformed file

cases.description: The schema file exists but contains malformed JSON. The factory should attempt to read it and propagate an IOException (or a subclass) indicating the parsing failure.

group: Fragment points to non‑existent definition

cases.description: The URI contains a fragment that refers to a definition that is not present in the loaded schema. The factory must detect the missing fragment and throw an IllegalArgumentException.

group: jsonNode is a primitive value – should raise IllegalArgumentException

cases.description: A JSON Schema must be a JSON object. Supplying a primitive JsonNode (e.g., a text node) should cause the factory to reject the input with an IllegalArgumentException.

group: SchemaLocation points to unreadable file – IOException

cases.description: The provided file URI does not exist or cannot be opened. Attempting to read the schema should result in an IOException.

group: Unsupported scheme ftp – IllegalArgumentException

cases.description: The factory only supports http, https, file and classpath schemes. Supplying an ftp URI should be rejected with an IllegalArgumentException.

group: jsonNode is a numeric primitive – should raise IllegalArgumentException

cases.description: A numeric JsonNode is not a valid schema object. The factory must throw an IllegalArgumentException when such a node is supplied.
